solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sick, boring, conceited malevolent guy

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: conceited means vain
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A description of a nasty man who is ill, dull and full of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked person, the bad man of a story with evil intentions.

clue.text: Politician isn't perceived badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: all thirteen letters, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A complaint that some politician goes unnoticed or is misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice president is a senior elected official, so an example of a politician.

clue.text: Lady Caroline went topless, looking radiant

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter is lost from the word it describes

blocks.note: Lady Caroline Lamb, the Regency novelist and lover of Byron
went with its first letter removed

explanation.surface: Lady Caroline Lamb, famously scandalous, went bare-chested and glowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Caroline Lamb was a Regency aristocrat notorious for her affair with Lord Byron.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that flickers softly or glows, so it is a synonym of radiant.

clue.text: Spy on chap last seen in Russia

indicators.note: the final letter seen in the following word is the one kept

blocks.note: the final letter of Russia
a chap is a gent

explanation.surface: A spy keeps watch on a man last spotted in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes before the chap; 'on' in a down clue loosely joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is someone working secretly for an intelligence service, a synonym for spy.

clue.text: Notorious criminal, leading member of Bush family?

blocks.note: surface reading: a prominent figure in the American political dynasty of the two President Bushes
setter's reading: the head of a gang that roamed the Australian bush, a notorious bushranger

explanation.surface: A notorious criminal suggested as head of the Bush political dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly led the Kelly Gang of bushrangers, outlaws of the Australian outback known as the bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Ned Kelly was a 19th-century Australian outlaw, famous for his home-made armour, so a notorious lawbreaker.

clue.text: Firms sadly not covering overhead expense

indicators.note: things going sadly are going wrong, so the letters are put out of order
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: not rearranged
CO is company, so firms are COS

explanation.surface: Companies regrettably fail to cover their running costs.
explanation.definitionFit: An oncost is an overhead, a running cost of a business beyond direct production costs.

clue.text: Royal family's gold coach seen in north London

blocks.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
Ange Postecoglou, the football coach who managed Tottenham Hotspur in north London

explanation.surface: A monarchy's golden state coach paraded through north London.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has'. Tottenham Hotspur is a north London football club, and Ange Postecoglou was its manager.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Orange-Nassau is the reigning royal dynasty of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Tory struggled to accept court reached guilty verdict

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative
struggled means competed, vied
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician fought the court's guilty finding.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury that convicted someone declared them guilty, so it delivered that finding.

clue.text: Drag school the French quietly pressure

blocks.note: SCH is an abbreviation for school
le is French for the
p, piano, is the musical instruction to play quietly
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: An instruction to haul a school along, putting gentle pressure on the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To schlepp, from Yiddish, is to haul or carry something heavy with effort, so to drag it.

clue.text: Digests clinic's last dopamine shot

indicators.note: the final letter of the possessive word is the only one taken
something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the final letter of clinic
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a clinic's final injection of a brain chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digests' looks like a verb about absorbing the shot, but it is a plural noun meaning summaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia, plural of compendium, are concise collections or summaries, which are also called digests.

clue.text: Visiting John, a humble prophet

indicators.note: a visitor stays inside a place for a time, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: A modest prophet calls on someone named John.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is a minor prophet of the Hebrew Bible, with a short book named after him.

clue.text: MAGA meme isn't working, Bannon finally admitted incompetence

indicators.note: working here means worked over or processed, so these letters are kneaded into a new order
finally points to the last letter of the name beside it
admitted means one extra letter is taken in to join the jumbled letters

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
the final letter of Bannon

explanation.surface: Steve Bannon concedes failure because a Trump slogan is not catching on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isn't working' reads as one phrase, but the letters of isn't belong to the fodder and 'working' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mismanagement is incompetent handling of affairs, so it names the incompetence.

clue.text: Nice not having hospital fold

indicators.note: not having something means going without it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: nice means pleasant
a san is a sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: The French city of Nice has no hospital to fall back on.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the city on the Riviera, but it is the everyday adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a doubled-over crease sewn into cloth, which is a kind of fold.

clue.text: Kitchen helpers with hourglass figures?

blocks.note: surface reading: shapely assistants working in a kitchen, with curvy waists
setter's reading: kitchen gadgets literally shaped like hourglasses, running sand to time cooking

explanation.surface: Curvaceous assistants helping out in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sand glasses that time boiled eggs are hourglass-shaped utensils used by cooks.

clue.text: Hospital department on which I depend wholly

blocks.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat
I rely, said of what one depends on

explanation.surface: Someone saying they are wholly reliant on a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely and wholly are synonyms, both meaning completely or fully.

clue.text: Cut antler off? Not keen!

indicators.note: something off has gone bad or wrong, so the letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked to saw off a deer's antler, someone declines.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant, so not eager to do something.

clue.text: First-class President of the United States to retire down south, in an ideal world

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the combined letters run backwards
south is knocked down, so the letter standing for south is dropped

blocks.note: A1 is first-class, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
the common acronym for the US president

explanation.surface: An excellent American president retiring to the South, as in a perfect world.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse the whole string, then remove the S (south) at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia, from Thomas More's book, is an imagined perfect society, so an ideal world.

clue.text: Worn out TV presenter broadcasting tripe

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: Dec is Declan Donnelly, of the British TV presenting duo Ant and Dec
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tired television host spouting nonsense on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a long-running British presenting double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means weakened by age or use, so dilapidated and worn out.

clue.text: Here in Paris occasionally called 'stalactite'

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only some evenly spaced letters are kept

blocks.note: ici is French for here
the first, third and fifth letters of called

explanation.surface: In Paris, a speaker sometimes refers to something as a stalactite.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of ice, formed like a stalactite in a cave from dripping water.

clue.text: Social medium not censoring content for the moment

indicators.note: censoring the content cuts out the middle, so only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: Insta is the casual name for Instagram
the outside letters of not

explanation.surface: A social media platform that, for now, is not censoring its posts.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a very brief point in time, the same as a moment.

clue.text: Very last letter from Greece describing tense blood-feud

indicators.note: in crossword use, to describe is to draw round, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
the last part is the end
eta is a Greek letter
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A final letter from Greece tells of a tense, long-running feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around something.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud between families, often involving revenge killings.

clue.text: Beat man having spectacular failure

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a king is a man, a piece in chess

explanation.surface: Defeat a man who is failing badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is used for a chess or draughts piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanking is slang for failing heavily, as a show or share price that collapses.

clue.text: Sirrah! Get thee north to the source of the Tweed!

indicators.note: going north in a down clue means travelling upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: an old contemptuous form of address to a man

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned command to a servant to go north to where the Tweed rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed meant is the cloth, not the river: Harris Tweed is woven in the Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris, in the Outer Hebrides, is where the famous handwoven Harris Tweed cloth originates.

clue.text: Piece of furniture having hackneyed appearance, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner was famed for swapping the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: hackneyed is cheesy and an appearance is an air; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A tired-looking old piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of cheesy air gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large comfortable upholstered armchair, an item of furniture.

clue.text: Build a barrier around marshland church

blocks.note: a fen is low marshy ground
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a wall around a church in the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: nothing goes inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To fence a place is to enclose it with a barrier such as railings or posts.

clue.text: Criminal following tech gazillionaire

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following
Elon Musk, the hugely rich tech entrepreneur

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker stalking a famous tech billionaire.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone convicted of a serious crime, so a criminal.

clue.text: Soup from Romanian city that's fit for a princess?

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes those letters from it

blocks.note: miso soup, the Japanese broth
Timisoara is a city in western Romania

explanation.surface: A soup from a Romanian city that would suit royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled half-crown worn by princesses, so a headpiece fit for one.

clue.text: Horrible, evil, super disgusting

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A string of words for something truly vile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible' looks like the definition, but it signals the rearrangement; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsive means arousing revulsion, so it is a close synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: Affirms second art gallery close to Thames

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
the Tate, the London art gallery
the final letter of Thames

explanation.surface: Someone declares a second art gallery sits near the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern and Tate Britain both stand beside the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to declare or assert it firmly, so states means affirms.

clue.text: Later this evening, little 'un nearly tucked in

indicators.note: something tucked in is placed snugly inside something else

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
nigh means nearly

explanation.surface: A small child is almost asleep, tucked into bed later this evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the coming evening or night of the present day.
